svg.title: Five Animal Architects, Five Building Materials
svg.desc: An illustrated atlas compares five real animal builders: a beaver's wooden and muddy lodge, a paper wasp's wood-and-saliva comb, a swallow's mud cup, a weaverbird's grass nest, and a honey bee's secreted wax comb. Material origins, original captions and institutional source mappings accompany each schematic. Drawings are not to scale.

svg.text: A SMALL ATLAS OF BUILT HOMES
Five species. Five ways to turn a material into a home.

g.text: Branches and mud collected; other material may occur.

text.tspan: A beaver can pile collected branches, sticks
and mud into a domed lodge. The shelter's
chamber sits above water, while an underwater
entrance connects it to the pond.

g.text: Collected fibres mixed with produced saliva.

text.tspan: This wasp chews collected wood fibres and adds
its own saliva, making papery pulp. It shapes
the mixture into an open comb of cells,
suspended beneath a protective overhang.

g.text: Collected mud and stems; grass and feather lining.

text.tspan: A pair may mould collected mud into a cup, often
reinforcing it with grass stems. Grass and
feathers soften the lining; the finished nest
can rest against a sheltered wall.

g.text: Collected strips; softer grass and feather lining.

text.tspan: A male weaves gathered grass or other leaf
strips into a hanging nest, usually with a
downward entrance. A female adds softer grass
and feathers after accepting the structure.

g.text: Natural cavity shown in cutaway; bees build the comb.
Collected resins (C) also contribute to nest sealing.

text.tspan: Workers secrete wax and shape it into hexagonal
comb cells that shelter developing young and
hold food. Elsewhere in the nest, collected
plant resins contribute to the sealing material
called propolis.

g.text: CELL MATERIAL ≠ EVERY MATERIAL IN THE NEST

svg.text: Schematic drawings, not to scale. Nest choices and material mixtures vary.
Institutional sources and direct claim mappings for all five entries are embedded in the SVG.
